Il carcinoma a cellule chiare è il tipo:
Clear cell carcinoma is the most common type (70-80%) of renal carcinoma. On CT it is typically hypervascular and heterogeneous, with intense enhancement in the corticomedullary phase and areas of necrosis, hemorrhage or cysts. Papillary carcinoma, by contrast, is homogeneous and hypovascular, and chromophobe has intermediate enhancement.
Staging (TNM): T1 ≤ 7 cm; T2 > 7 cm limited to the kidney; T3a perirenal or sinus fat or renal vein, T3b cava below the diaphragm, T3c cava above the diaphragm; T4 beyond Gerota's fascia or ipsilateral adrenal gland by contiguity. Typical metastases: lung (multiple nodules, also "cannonball"), lymph nodes, bone (lytic), liver, adrenal gland, brain, pancreas.
In selected metastatic patients, cytoreductive nephrectomy is discussed together with systemic therapy.
Davanti a una massa renale guarda sempre: In front of a renal mass always look at the renal vein, cava, lymph nodes, adrenal glands, bone and lung bases.
